question: Why do safe motherhood programs pay close attention to maternal morbidity alongside mortality?

options.A: To prevent long-term suffering and disability in women who survive
options.B: Because pregnancy illnesses are much easier to treat than pregnancy deaths
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of operating maternity wards
options.D: To ensure accurate record keeping for government health insurance

explanation: Looking at morbidity helps us protect and restore the quality of life for mothers who make it through tough complications. Every survivor deserves full healing!

question: Why is maintaining a patient's mobility considered vital for overall health?

options.A: It shortens the required hospital stay to one day
options.B: It guarantees complete recovery from any surgery
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for pain medication
options.D: It supports circulation and preserves muscle mass

explanation: Movement keeps blood flowing properly and prevents muscles from weakening quickly during illness or recovery. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T8#GNS324_U3_T8_h1)

question: Why is taking a nighttime dose of a cystine-binding medication so important?

options.A: Cystine excretion often peaks at night during periods of sleep and dehydration
options.B: Kidney blood flow drops to zero during deep sleep, requiring higher drug levels
options.C: Bedtime dosing completely eliminates the need for daytime water intake
options.D: The liver metabolizes the medication much faster during daylight hours

explanation: At night, we sleep without drinking water, making our urine concentrated. A bedtime dose protects the kidneys during those vulnerable overnight hours!

question: Why is putting way too many overlapping lines on a single graph a bad idea?

options.A: It violates international laws regarding hospital record keeping.
options.B: It prevents the horizontal axis from showing future time intervals.
options.C: It creates an unreadable tangle of ink that defeats the purpose of a visual aid.
options.D: It automatically changes the numerical values of the raw data.

explanation: Exactly! Graphs are supposed to make data clear and simple. Too many lines just create a messy web that is impossible to read.

question: How has flight nursing changed from the old days to modern times?

options.A: It changed from using airplanes to using boats exclusively
options.B: It stopped focusing on patient stability during flight
options.C: It shifted from basic transport to mobile intensive care
options.D: It moved from caring for civilians to only caring for soldiers

explanation: Exactly! While it used to be mostly about just moving patients from point A to point B, today's flight nurses bring full ICU-level care right up into the skies.

question: Which part of the teenage brain is still maturing and plays a big role in impulse control and risk-taking?

options.A: Cerebellum
options.B: Occipital lobe
options.C: Prefrontal cortex
options.D: Medulla oblongata

explanation: Correct! The prefrontal cortex develops slowly into early adulthood, which explains why teenagers sometimes struggle with weighing long-term consequences.

question: A patient sits still in a chair for many hours on a long flight. Which mechanism for venous return is temporarily reduced?

options.A: Skeletal muscle pump
options.B: Aortic valve recoil
options.C: Renal blood filtration
options.D: Coronary artery perfusion

explanation: Without leg movement, the skeletal muscle pump cannot help push venous blood upward, which can lead to pooling. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h5)

question: What is the purpose of a cough stress test during a physical checkup?

options.A: To check if coughing triggers a bladder spasm
options.B: To test the strength of the patient's respiratory muscles
options.C: To measure lung capacity while the patient lies flat
options.D: To observe if physical pressure causes immediate urine leakage

explanation: By asking the patient to cough, the clinician can watch directly to see if pressure causes any accidental leakage.

question: Which main muscle forms the wall of the urinary bladder and stretches as it fills up with urine?

options.A: Trigone muscle
options.B: Detrusor muscle
options.C: Dartos muscle
options.D: Cremaster muscle

explanation: You've got this! The detrusor muscle is the big muscular wall of the bladder that stretches out nicely to hold urine until you're ready to go.

question: Which ethical principle refers to the nurse's core duty to do no harm to patients?

options.A: Beneficence
options.B: Justice
options.C: Non-maleficence
options.D: Autonomy

explanation: Great nursing foundation here! 'Non-maleficence' literally means avoiding any physical, emotional, or psychological harm to the patients in your care.

question: What should a nurse focus on when assessing a pregnant patient for constipation?

options.A: The blood pressure reading taken in the right arm
options.B: Exclusively the heartbeat of the developing fetus
options.C: Stool consistency, straining effort, and dietary habits
options.D: Only the exact weight of the patient on the scale

explanation: Spot on! To truly help, we need to ask about how hard the stool is, if she struggles to push, and what she's been eating and drinking.

question: Why is oral rehydration salt (ORS) solution preferred over plain water for rehydration?

options.A: It tastes much sweeter so children will drink large amounts quickly
options.B: It contains strong antibiotics that kill bacteria inside the stomach
options.C: It contains a specific ratio of glucose and sodium that enhances water absorption
options.D: It numbs the stomach lining to stop painful vomiting right away

explanation: The sodium-glucose cotransport mechanism in the intestine uses glucose to pull sodium and water back into the bloodstream effectively. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h5)

question: Why can blood protein markers like albumin sometimes give misleading results during an infection?

options.A: Infection causes the liver to permanently stop producing all plasma proteins
options.B: Dehydration artificially raises albumin levels to mask underlying deficiencies
options.C: Inflammation lowers their levels independently of actual dietary protein intake
options.D: White blood cells consume circulating albumin for energy during fever

explanation: When the body is inflamed, it triggers an immune response that drops blood protein levels, even if the patient's diet is fine. Tricky, but good to know!

question: Why is prioritization necessary after collecting community health data?

options.A: Government regulations forbid treating more than one disease at a time
options.B: Minor health issues are completely unimportant and should be ignored forever
options.C: It helps nurses avoid doing any field work for the rest of the year
options.D: Resources like time and money are limited, so the most urgent issues must be tackled first

explanation: Because resources are finite, prioritization ensures the most pressing and impactful health problems receive attention first. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h6)

question: How can long-term fatigue lead to physical deconditioning?

options.A: Fatigue triggers the rapid breakdown of calcium in the long bones.
options.B: Exhaustion forces the heart muscle to beat at twice its normal speed constantly.
options.C: Lack of energy leads to inactivity, causing muscle weakness and reduced stamina.
options.D: Continuous resting stops the digestive tract from absorbing dietary proteins.

explanation: Makes sense, right? When you're too tired to move around, your muscles don't get used. Over time, they weaken, making everyday activities feel even harder.

question: Why are elderly individuals at higher risk for severe burn injuries from hot water?

options.A: Their skin is thinner and loses sensitivity
options.B: They prefer much hotter bath temperatures
options.C: Their homes lack modern plumbing systems
options.D: They spend more time cooking than younger adults

explanation: Thinning skin and reduced nerve sensitivity mean older adults may not feel extreme heat quickly enough to pull away. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T4#GNS324_U6_T4_h4)

question: A community refuses to use a newly drilled borehole because the water tastes different from their stream. What is the best IEC approach for a nurse to take?

options.A: Tell the villagers they are being stubborn and must use the borehole immediately.
options.B: Respect their concern, investigate the water safety, and explain the health benefits through dialogue.
options.C: Punish village leaders by withholding malaria medications from the local clinic.
options.D: Close the borehole permanently and force them to walk back to the stream.

explanation: Effective IEC involves listening to community concerns, validating their observations, and addressing them respectfully rather than using force. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T2#GNS124_U5_T2_h3)

question: What is the best response when a nurse makes a pure human error due to a slip or tiredness?

options.A: Report the nurse directly to the national licensing board
options.B: Suspend the nurse immediately without pay for negligence
options.C: Force the nurse to complete mandatory disciplinary training
options.D: Console the nurse and check the system for flaws

explanation: Everyone makes honest slips when tired. Punishing a pure accident doesn't help—fixing the system does!

question: A patient presents with symmetrical numbness and a 'stocking-glove' tingling pattern in both feet and hands. Which classification of neuropathy best fits this clinical picture?

options.A: Polyneuropathy
options.B: Mononeuropathy
options.C: Radiculopathy
options.D: Mononeuritis multiplex

explanation: Widespread, symmetrical involvement that starts in the extremities and moves inward is the classic presentation of a systemic polyneuropathy. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T18#GNS222_U3_T18_h2)

question: Why do nurses strictly track and count surgical swabs before closing a wound?

options.A: To prevent dangerous retained items inside the patient
options.B: To calculate the exact duration of the surgical procedure
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of hospital materials
options.D: To ensure the theater team finishes their shift early

explanation: Patient safety first! Counting every single swab ensures nothing is accidentally left behind inside the patient's body cavity.

question: As a nurse, what is your key responsibility when giving medications for hormone disorders?

options.A: Monitoring for expected therapeutic effects and potential adverse reactions
options.B: Prohibiting the patient from eating any food for 48 hours
options.C: Prescribing the initial starting dosage based on daily weight
options.D: Manufacturing synthetic hormone replacements in the hospital pharmacy

explanation: Exactly! You are the patient's safety net—watching closely to see if the drug is helping and checking for any scary side effects.

question: What unusual sign might a patient on long-term steroids show when they catch an infection?

options.A: Low-grade fever
options.B: Rapid pus formation
options.C: Extreme high fever
options.D: Severe joint swelling

explanation: Because steroids quiet down the immune system, classic loud warning signs like a blazing high fever or heavy swelling might be hidden. A low-grade fever might be all you see!

question: Why must school management set aside specific funds in their yearly budget for health?

options.A: To purchase luxury furniture for administrative offices
options.B: To pay for students' personal family medical bills
options.C: To purchase medical supplies and maintain health facilities
options.D: To fund international educational excursions

explanation: You nailed it! Having dedicated funds means first-aid items, cleaning products, and clinic tools are always ready when emergencies happen.

question: What is the crucial next step a patient must take right after using an emergency epinephrine auto-injector?

options.A: Lie flat on the floor with their feet elevated for two hours
options.B: Call their primary clinic doctor to schedule a routine follow-up
options.C: Go to the nearest hospital emergency room for evaluation
options.D: Take a strong oral antihistamine pill to prevent rebound

explanation: Spot on! Always head to the hospital. A secondary (biphasic) reaction can pop up hours later, and medical observation keeps the patient safe.

question: A 14-year-old pregnant patient faces a high nutritional risk. Why does this happen during her pregnancy?

options.A: Complete resistance to iron supplementation
options.B: Direct competition for nutrients between her growing body and the fetus
options.C: Permanent storage overload of water-soluble vitamins
options.D: Immediate cessation of all bone mineral absorption

explanation: Exactly! Since a young teenager is still growing herself, her body and the baby have to share and compete for limited nutrients.

question: What is the best way to respond when a grieving family member is crying silently at the bedside?

options.A: Leave the room immediately so they can cry alone
options.B: Remind them that everything happens for a reason
options.C: Sit quietly nearby and offer a supportive physical presence
options.D: Tell a cheerful story to distract them from their sadness

explanation: A quiet, supportive presence shows you care and validates their pain without forcing awkward talk or empty clichés.

question: How does the strict criminalization of abortion in Nigeria directly affect patient health outcomes?

options.A: It encourages traditional healers to adopt modern sterile surgical techniques
options.B: It guarantees that all post-abortion patients receive free government care
options.C: It forces patients to seek secretive care, leading to dangerous treatment delays
options.D: It completely eliminates the practice of illegal pregnancy terminations

explanation: Because of fear of arrest, women often hide what they've done and only come to the hospital when complications become life-threatening. Compassionate, confidential nursing care can help break down this fear!

question: When must you clean your hands when wearing gloves?

options.A: Only when the gloves look dirty or torn
options.B: After removing them, but never before
options.C: Before putting them on and after taking them off
options.D: Only before putting on a fresh pair

explanation: Always wash or sanitize your hands before donning gloves and right after doffing them! Gloves can get tiny tears, and your hands can easily pick up germs during removal.

question: What makes animal protein stand out nutritionally compared to most plant proteins?

options.A: They are always lower in financial cost than plant foods
options.B: They never contain any traces of dietary fat
options.C: They contain all the essential amino acids the body cannot make
options.D: They contain high amounts of complex dietary fiber

explanation: You got it! Animal proteins are complete proteins because they supply every single essential amino acid your body needs but can't manufacture on its own.

question: What should be a nurse's main focus when giving diet advice to a low-income family?

options.A: Advising them to eat only once every two days
options.B: Recommending affordable, locally available foods
options.C: Telling them to stop eating traditional family meals
options.D: Insisting they purchase expensive imported vitamins

explanation: Good nutrition advice has to be practical. Always recommend foods that the family can easily find and afford in their local market.

question: How long must a seizure last continuously to be called status epilepticus?

options.A: More than two hours
options.B: Exactly one minute
options.C: Thirty continuous minutes
options.D: More than five minutes

explanation: Status epilepticus is a medical emergency defined as continuous seizure activity lasting longer than five minutes. Quick thinking saves lives here!

question: In simple terms, what is osmosis?

options.A: The active pumping of mineral particles out of a cell using energy
options.B: The settling of heavy mineral solutes at the bottom of a container
options.C: The movement of blood cells through tiny capillary walls
options.D: The movement of water across a membrane toward higher solute concentration

explanation: Spot on! Water naturally moves toward areas with more solutes (like salt or sugar) to try and balance things out. Water always follows where the crowd is thickest!

question: What is the name of the most common expectorant you'll see in everyday pharmacy practice?

options.A: Diphenhydramine
options.B: Salbutamol
options.C: Guaifenesin
options.D: Dextromethorphan

explanation: That's it! Guaifenesin is the go-to active ingredient in almost all chest congestion syrups you see on the shelves.

question: Which type of diseases must be reported the absolute fastest because they can spark sudden outbreaks?

options.A: Routine dental health issues
options.B: Epidemic-prone diseases
options.C: Surgical complication records
options.D: Chronic nutritional deficiencies

explanation: Diseases like cholera or measles move fast! We call these epidemic-prone, and they need immediate reporting so we can protect the community.

question: What key fact should nurses explain to adolescents about emergency contraceptive pills?

options.A: They provide full immunity against all known sexually transmitted diseases
options.B: They must be taken every single morning to maintain long-term effectiveness
options.C: They guarantee that future menstrual cycles will arrive on the exact same day
options.D: They do not interrupt an established pregnancy or act as an abortifacient

explanation: Emergency contraceptives simply delay ovulation; they don't harm an egg that has already implanted.

question: Why is a severe lack of vitamin B1 (thiamine) a major worry in hyperemesis?

options.A: It directly causes sudden gestational diabetes in the second trimester
options.B: It triggers immediate placental abruption and severe bleeding
options.C: It can lead to serious neurological issues like Wernicke's encephalopathy
options.D: It stops the production of amniotic fluid completely

explanation: Starvation and vomiting deplete vitamin B1, which can trigger confusion and nerve issues known as Wernicke's encephalopathy. Knowing this helps you protect your patients early!

question: At what point should waste sorting (segregation) happen in the clinical ward?

options.A: At the end of the nursing shift
options.B: When the cleaner arrives with large trucks
options.C: After the waste reaches the municipal dump
options.D: Immediately at the point of generation

explanation: Spot on! Sorting waste right where you use it prevents dangerous mix-ups and keeps everyone handling it safe.

question: Why is the nurse's role so crucial for making a National Drug Policy work in real life?

options.A: Nurses are solely responsible for importing essential medicines from international manufacturers.
options.B: Nurses are the frontline professionals who handle, administer, and educate patients about medications daily.
options.C: Nurses hold the legal authority to shut down illegal open-air drug markets across the country.
options.D: Nurses write the legal statutes that govern pharmaceutical practice in government courts.

explanation: Policies are just paper until we put them into practice! Because nurses handle, give, and teach about drugs every day, our actions make the policy a success.

question: When is the best time to discuss family planning options with a patient receiving post-abortion care?

options.A: Before the patient is discharged from the clinical setting
options.B: Only after the patient experiences a second unplanned pregnancy
options.C: Refer them to a distant pharmacy without discussing options
options.D: Wait until six months have passed to avoid overwhelming them

explanation: Spot on! Bringing up family planning before discharge ensures the patient is protected against a quick repeat pregnancy while they are still connected to care.

question: How do most medications pass from a nursing mother's blood into her breast milk?

options.A: Cellular phagocytosis
options.B: Active transport pumps
options.C: Passive diffusion
options.D: Direct ductal injection

explanation: Just like with the placenta, drugs usually drift naturally across membranes into breast milk based on concentration and fat solubility.

question: Why do doctors often order a full blood count (FBC) for a patient with heavy periods (menorrhagia)?

options.A: To look for a bacterial infection in the uterus
options.B: To see if the patient might get gestational diabetes
options.C: To check the levels of progesterone and estrogen
options.D: To check for low blood iron (anemia) caused by blood loss

explanation: Spot on! Heavy monthly bleeding can slowly drain the body's iron stores, leading to iron-deficiency anemia that needs our nursing care.

question: What is the most effective way for nurses to help prevent unsafe abortions in the community?

options.A: Providing accessible family planning education and modern contraception
options.B: Reporting all suspected cases of premarital sex to local community elders
options.C: Enforcing strict hospital visitation limits for young unmarried females
options.D: Promoting traditional herbal remedies as safe alternatives for fertility control

explanation: The best cure is prevention! When young people have easy access to modern family planning and accurate education, the rate of unintended pregnancies—and unsafe abortions—drops dramatically.

question: A nurse wants to understand why mothers in a village refuse to bring children for immunization. Which method is most suitable?

options.A: Focus group discussion with mothers
options.B: Checking the expiration dates of vaccine vials
options.C: Measuring the mid-upper arm circumference of infants
options.D: Counting the number of houses in the ward

explanation: Group discussions allow community members to freely share cultural beliefs, fears, and reasons behind specific health behaviors. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of the Vaughan Williams classification system for nurses?

options.A: To group antiarrhythmic drugs by their primary electrophysiological effect on the heart
options.B: To determine the financial cost and manufacturing source of cardiac drugs
options.C: To calculate the exact safe dosage of medication based on patient body weight
options.D: To predict which patients will develop permanent heart failure within a year

explanation: The classification organizes drugs by how they alter the electrical currents and action potentials in cardiac tissue. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h2)

question: How can pregnant women hold onto extra water and sodium without their blood pressure shooting up?

options.A: Renal tubules stop working completely in the second trimester.
options.B: The heart pumps with a much weaker force.
options.C: Excess fluid is immediately stored in the amniotic sac.
options.D: Systemic vascular resistance decreases at the same time.

explanation: Blood vessels relax and widen during pregnancy, giving the extra fluid plenty of room so blood pressure stays nice and stable.

question: You want to start an immunization campaign in a rural town. What should be your very first step?

options.A: Consult with local leaders and respect community values
options.B: Import expensive foreign medications without checking needs
options.C: Call the police to force every parent to bring their child
options.D: Build a brand-new private hospital without telling residents

explanation: Spot on! Working hand-in-hand with local leaders builds immediate trust and ensures the community happily joins in to protect their health.

question: Which group of organs gets drugs distributed to them the fastest because of high blood supply?

options.A: Ligaments and tendons
options.B: Bones and resting muscle
options.C: Heart, brain, and liver
options.D: Skin and fatty tissue

explanation: Vial organs get a huge share of the blood pumped by the heart, meaning circulating drugs arrive there almost instantly!

question: What simple question did Bernardino Ramazzini say doctors must always ask their patients?

options.A: What is your occupation?
options.B: How many hours do you sleep?
options.C: Where do you buy your food?
options.D: What is your family medical history?

explanation: Ramazzini realized that a patient's job is often the biggest clue to what is making them sick. Always remember to check your patient's work background!

question: What causes sharp, stabbing round ligament pain on the sides of the abdomen during pregnancy?

options.A: Infection of the urinary bladder lining
options.B: Stretching of the ligaments supporting the growing uterus
options.C: Rapid drop in maternal blood pressure
options.D: Spasms of the intestinal smooth muscle

explanation: Round ligament pain happens when these supporting structures stretch rapidly to accommodate the enlarging uterus. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T014#GNS226_U2_T014_h2)

question: When you get a cut, your body triggers blood clotting where each step activates even more clotting. What kind of loop is this?

options.A: Negative feedback
options.B: Adaptive atrophy
options.C: Homeostatic breakdown
options.D: Positive feedback

explanation: Spot on! Positive feedback pushes a process forward until a goal is reached—like forming a solid clot to stop bleeding before it slows down.

question: What is closed-loop communication in a clinical setting?

options.A: Talking only through written memos left in a locked box
options.B: The receiver repeats the instruction back to confirm understanding
options.C: Using encrypted messaging apps for all doctor handovers
options.D: Restricting conversations to the nurse's station only

explanation: Closed-loop communication stops dangerous mistakes by ensuring the sender hears the exact message echoed back accurately. [learn more](GST321_U1_T13#GST321_U1_T13_h4)

question: Which of these is an example of structural mitigation in a hospital?

options.A: Teaching community members how to wash their hands
options.B: Bolting heavy oxygen tanks securely to the wall
options.C: Writing a new policy on emergency communication
options.D: Conducting a fire drill for the nursing staff

explanation: You nailed it! Structural mitigation involves making physical changes to buildings or equipment to keep people safe.

question: What defines direct contact transmission?

options.A: Carrying of pathogens by biting insects like mosquitoes
options.B: Inhalation of tiny dried respiratory droplets floating in the air
options.C: Spread of germs through contaminated drinking water supplies
options.D: Physical transfer of pathogens between an infected person and a susceptible host

explanation: Direct contact requires physical touch or direct exposure to bodily fluids without any intermediary objects or surfaces. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T6#GNS313_U1_T6_h3)

question: Beyond physical checks, what is another crucial part of postpartum care for a mother who just had twins or triplets?

options.A: Encouraging the mother to return to work within two weeks
options.B: Restricting family visits to prevent the mother from talking
options.C: Providing emotional support and connecting them with practical resources
options.D: Insisting that the mother cares for the newborns entirely on her own

explanation: Well done! Raising more than one baby at once can feel overwhelming. Offering kind words and connecting families to helper networks is a huge part of great nursing care.

question: A patient collapses in the hospital ward. What should the nurse do right after confirming the patient is unresponsive and not breathing normally?

options.A: Leave the patient to find a doctor
options.B: Call for help and activate the emergency response
options.C: Administer rescue breaths through a mask
options.D: Start chest compressions immediately

explanation: Activating the emergency team immediately ensures that extra hands and equipment like an AED are on the way. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T1#GNS212_U2_T1_h3)

question: What is a common challenge home health nurses face in many Nigerian cities?

options.A: Logistical delays caused by traffic congestion and poor road infrastructure
options.B: Strict hospital rules that forbid nurses from leaving the wards
options.C: Excessive government funding that complicates financial paperwork
options.D: An oversupply of advanced medical equipment in private houses

explanation: So true! Navigating Lagos or city traffic and bad roads can make getting to home visits quite an adventure.

question: What does it mean when a disease is described as 'endemic' in a community?

options.A: It only affects travellers visiting from foreign countries
options.B: It appears once every ten years and then vanishes
options.C: It is constantly present at a steady baseline level
options.D: It suddenly affects people across multiple continents

explanation: Think of an endemic disease as a constant visitor—it stays within a specific area consistently over time without needing a fresh introduction from outside. You've got this!

question: What is the primary physical form of medication delivered by a nebulizer to the patient's lungs?

options.A: A compressed gas tablet
options.B: A fine mist or aerosolized vapor
options.C: A warm liquid solution
options.D: A dry powder capsule

explanation: A nebulizer turns liquid medicine into a vapor so the patient can easily breathe it deep into the lungs. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h1)

question: What is a major clinical benefit of Long-Acting Reversible Contraception (LARC) for teenagers?

options.A: They provide permanent sterilization after five years
options.B: They can be inserted independently by the user at home
options.C: They eliminate all risks of contracting viral STIs
options.D: They do not require daily compliance to remain effective

explanation: Once a LARC is placed by a clinician, it works quietly in the background for years without daily effort from the client.

question: What does it mean when a cancer cell is called 'poorly differentiated'?

options.A: The cancer cells look very different from normal tissue cells
options.B: The tumor cells have stopped growing completely
options.C: The cells are surrounded by a thick protective capsule
options.D: The mass is unable to attract a blood supply

explanation: Well done! 'Differentiated' means looking like the original tissue. Poorly differentiated cells have lost their specialized look, which usually means the cancer is more aggressive.

question: When giving a bed bath, what is the golden rule for the direction of washing?

options.A: From the feet upward toward the face
options.B: From the left side of the body to the right side
options.C: From the back of the body to the front
options.D: From cleanest areas to dirtiest areas

explanation: Always wash from clean to dirty! This simple habit stops germs from spreading from high-contamination zones, like the perineum, up to sensitive areas like the face.

question: Why is it important to rest your fingers against the patient's cheek while holding the otoscope?

options.A: To block out bright room lighting for a clearer visual field
options.B: To prevent injury to the ear canal if the patient suddenly moves
options.C: To keep the otoscope battery handle from becoming disconnected
options.D: To warm up the speculum before it touches the sensitive skin

explanation: Bracing your hand on their cheek is a brilliant safety trick. If the patient jerks or moves, your hand moves with them, protecting the delicate ear canal!

question: How many daily medications do doctors usually mean when they talk about polypharmacy?

options.A: Taking two or more medications daily
options.B: Taking ten or more medications daily
options.C: Taking only herbal remedies alongside drugs
options.D: Taking five or more medications daily

explanation: You'll often hear this in the ward! Polypharmacy simply means a patient is taking five or more regular medications at the same time.

question: What is the maximum recommended time limit for a single intubation attempt to protect the patient?

options.A: 30 seconds
options.B: 5 minutes
options.C: 2 minutes
options.D: 10 minutes

explanation: Limiting attempts to 30 seconds prevents prolonged interruption of oxygen delivery and avoids severe hypoxia. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h4)

question: Why do complex birth defects require a whole team of different specialists?

options.A: Surgeons aren't allowed to talk to parents alone
options.B: Special machines can only be run by top administrators
options.C: Hospital rules require ten doctors to sign off
options.D: The condition affects multiple body systems needing different expert skills

explanation: When a baby's heart, breathing, feeding, and movement are all involved, it takes a village of experts working together to give the best care!

question: What is the main foundation of public health when looking at nutrition?

options.A: High-dose antibiotic use
options.B: Regular surgical screening
options.C: Adequate nutrition
options.D: Frequent vaccination

explanation: Great job! Eating proper food gives the body the energy it needs to stay healthy and fight off sickness, which is why it forms the bedrock of public health.

question: Why does early teenage pregnancy often negatively impact a young person's future?

options.A: It directly impairs cognitive functioning and memory
options.B: It automatically causes permanent physical disability in all young mothers
options.C: It frequently interrupts their education and limits economic opportunities
options.D: It permanently removes all support from their extended families

explanation: Parenthood during adolescence often forces teenagers to drop out of school, making it much harder to gain the skills needed for stable employment later in life. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T9#GNS312_U3_T9_h1)

question: How do extrinsic rewards (like cash bonuses or awards) usually affect nurses over time?

options.A: They work exclusively on administrative staff rather than clinicians
options.B: They permanently alter a nurse's core professional values
options.C: They provide effective short-term drive but may lose impact over time
options.D: They completely eliminate the need for supportive workplace leadership

explanation: External perks are nice, but people eventually get used to them. That's why relying only on bonuses isn't enough for long-term happiness at work.

question: What is the main goal of adding social inclusion into nursing care plans?

options.A: To ensure that all hospital beds are filled by patients from identical backgrounds
options.B: To eliminate the need for physicians to write formal medical prescriptions
options.C: To empower vulnerable patients and reduce health disparities caused by social inequality
options.D: To force patients to change their cultural and religious beliefs before discharge

explanation: Social inclusion in nursing is all about making sure everyone gets fair, respectful care by tackling the root causes of discrimination and helping patients speak for themselves.

question: Based on how much the body needs them, what are the two main groups of nutrients?

options.A: Macronutrients and micronutrients
options.B: Proteins and carbohydrates
options.C: Organic and inorganic nutrients
options.D: Vitamins and minerals

explanation: You got this! We split nutrients into macronutrients (needed in large amounts like carbs and proteins) and micronutrients (needed in small amounts like vitamins).

question: Why do nurses need to speak up and do advocacy work alongside regular bedside care?

options.A: Patients will refuse medications unless nurses also lobby local leaders
options.B: Hospital management requires nurses to submit weekly political reports
options.C: Clinical care alone cannot fix underlying systemic gaps causing illness
options.D: Clinical nursing duties do not take up enough of a nurse's work shift

explanation: Great thinking! Treating patients at the bedside is vital, but if bad living conditions or broken policies keep making people sick, we have to advocate for wider changes too.

question: Which major artery brings the main blood supply to the external male genitalia?

options.A: Common iliac artery
options.B: Internal pudendal artery
options.C: Renal artery
options.D: Femoral artery

explanation: The internal pudendal artery is the main highway delivering rich, oxygenated blood straight to the structures of the penis and scrotum.

question: How do poverty and transport delays worsen severe maternal illness in local communities?

options.A: They stop the fetus from growing properly inside the amniotic sac
options.B: They directly cause the placenta to detach prematurely from the uterine wall
options.C: They lower the normal blood pressure of the mother below safe levels
options.D: They prevent timely access to skilled medical care during emergencies

explanation: When transport is hard to find or money is tight, simple delays can turn a manageable emergency into a life-threatening situation. This is a huge focus in community health nursing!

question: Why is it important to tailor teaching to a patient's literacy and language level?

options.A: It speeds up the nursing documentation process at the end of the shift
options.B: Federal laws prohibit speaking medical terminology in private homes
options.C: It ensures the patient can truly understand and follow self-care steps
options.D: Patients with low literacy cannot operate any form of medical equipment

explanation: Education only works if the patient understands it; matching their language and literacy ensures they can manage their condition safely. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T7#GNS324_U1_T7_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a safe or recommended way to lower your risk of getting an STI?

options.A: Receiving available prophylactic vaccinations against viral pathogens
options.B: Using barrier methods like condoms consistently and correctly
options.C: Relying solely on herbal supplements to block infection transmission
options.D: Undergoing routine periodic STI screenings with new or multiple partners

explanation: Herbal mixtures won't stop an STI! Safe practices mean using condoms, getting vaccinated, and going for regular checks.

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do when starting a Behavioural Change Communication project?

options.A: Evaluating final program financial costs
options.B: Punishing non-compliant community members
options.C: Assessment and formative research
options.D: Mass media television broadcasting

explanation: Correct! Before designing any messages, you have to talk to the community to find out what they already know and what they actually need.

question: Why must the hole on the skin barrier be measured to fit just a tiny bit larger than the stoma?

options.A: To allow for the natural shrinking of the stoma over many years
options.B: To prevent the barrier from rubbing against and injuring the stoma tissue
options.C: To give extra space for air to circulate under the pouch
options.D: To make it easier to empty liquid waste from the bottom

explanation: You nailed it! Cutting the opening slightly larger protects the delicate stoma tissue from painful friction while keeping the skin safe.

question: Before you walk up to patients in a ward to chat with them for a study, what must you secure first?

options.A: Permission from the patient's family members only
options.B: A personal loan from the hospital bank
options.C: Formal institutional and ethical approval
options.D: Complete control over hospital bed assignments

explanation: You got it! Protecting patients is our number one priority. Ethical clearance is non-negotiable before any research begins.

question: What is the main reason we do a bladder irrigation?

options.A: To stimulate voluntary control of the urethral sphincter
options.B: To measure the exact total daily kidney function
options.C: To permanently cure chronic urinary tract infections
options.D: To wash away debris and keep the catheter open

explanation: You're doing great! Flushing out small clots and sediment keeps urine flowing smoothly so the tube doesn't get blocked.

question: What is a common myth that stops people from using family planning in many communities?

options.A: Family planning guarantees you will have a baby boy
options.B: Contraceptives are made only by local farmers
options.C: Using a condom cures all infections instantly
options.D: Modern contraceptives cause permanent infertility

explanation: You nailed it! A lot of people fear that using birth control now means they won't be able to bear children later, which isn't true.

question: If a brain tumor starts growing inside the skull, what has to happen first to keep pressure from rising too high?

options.A: Brain neurons must shrink in size to increase internal air pockets.
options.B: The bones of the skull must stretch outward to create more space.
options.C: Cerebrospinal fluid or blood volume must decrease to compensate.
options.D: Systemic heart rate must drop to zero to halt blood entering the head.

explanation: Since an adult skull cannot stretch, the body makes room for the new mass by pushing out some CSF or blood.

question: What is the most common reason an unconscious adult lying flat on their back stops breathing well?

options.A: The tiny air sacs in the lungs collapse
options.B: Their tongue falls backward and blocks the throat
options.C: Thick mucus builds up in the windpipe
options.D: The bronchial tubes go into a sudden spasm

explanation: When someone passes out, their muscles relax completely. Gravity takes over, causing the lower jaw and tongue to slump backward and block the pharynx.

question: What is the main job of the arachnoid granulations?

options.A: To supply strong structural support between skull bones
options.B: To allow cerebrospinal fluid to return to the venous blood
options.C: To manufacture fresh blood cells for the central nervous system
options.D: To anchor the spinal cord firmly to the vertebral column

explanation: You're doing great. These little structures act like drainage valves, letting used cerebrospinal fluid flow safely back into the bloodstream.

question: What is the main reason pregnant women experience heartburn?

options.A: Increased production of hydrochloric acid in the stomach
options.B: Relaxation of the lower esophageal sphincter by progesterone
options.C: Rapid enlargement of the liver pressing on the diaphragm
options.D: Frequent consumption of spicy foods during meals

explanation: Progesterone relaxes the valve right at the top of the stomach, letting acid sneak up into the food pipe (esophagus) and cause that burning feeling.

question: Which of these is NOT a common physical barrier for people with disabilities in public buildings?

options.A: Wide automatic sliding entrance doors
options.B: Absence of functional elevators in multi-story buildings
options.C: Narrow doorways that block wheelchairs
options.D: High staircases without accompanying ramps

explanation: Spot on! Wide sliding doors actually make life easier and more accessible, unlike stairs and narrow doors.

question: A teenage boy asks why his voice is cracking and getting deeper. What is the cause?

options.A: Weakening of the throat muscles during physical exercise
options.B: Temporary irritation of the airway from rapid lung growth
options.C: Growth and thickening of the vocal cords due to testosterone
options.D: Swelling of the tonsils caused by common adolescent infections

explanation: Correct! As testosterone levels rise, the larynx and vocal cords grow larger and thicker, which naturally drops the pitch of the voice.

question: What is the best position for your patient during a thoracentesis?

options.A: Lying flat on the back with arms raised above the head
options.B: Sitting upright and leaning forward over a bedside table
options.C: Positioned flat on the unaffected side with knees bent
options.D: Prone with a pillow placed directly under the abdomen

explanation: Awesome! This forward-leaning posture opens up the spaces between the ribs nicely, making it much safer and easier for the doctor to reach the fluid.

question: Why must flight nurses be great at making quick, independent decisions?

options.A: They operate far away from immediate physician backup
options.B: Flight nurses work completely alone without any crew members
options.C: Pilots are not allowed to talk to medical staff
options.D: Hospitals do not provide guidelines for patient care

explanation: Spot on! Up in the air, you often don't have a doctor standing next to you, so flight nurses must trust their training and act fast.

question: As a community health nurse, why must you look at environmental factors when assessing a patient's stress?

options.A: Environmental triggers are the only proven cause of mental illness
options.B: External pressures like security and poverty often drive individual stress
options.C: Individual counseling works without knowing the community background
options.D: Nurses are required to fix bad roads and public infrastructure

explanation: An individual's stress rarely happens in a vacuum. Shared hardships like poverty or safety issues play a huge role in how they feel.

question: Which Nigerian law provides key legal protections against child abuse and exploitation?

options.A: The Federal Highway Traffic Code
options.B: The National Tax Administration Act
options.C: The Petroleum Industry Act
options.D: The Child Rights Act

explanation: Great job! The Child Rights Act is the foundational law that protects minors across Nigeria.

question: What is a major reason why children end up roaming the streets in many communities?

options.A: Excessive participation in organized school sports
options.B: Severe poverty and financial hardship at home
options.C: Strict adherence to traditional cultural values
options.D: Overabundance of free government-provided housing

explanation: Spot on. Extreme financial hardship at home often forces families to send children out to find money, leaving them exposed and vulnerable on the streets.

question: As a nurse, what is a key care step for a patient being treated for polycythaemia?

options.A: Giving high-dose iron with meals
options.B: Restricting all physical movement to bed rest
options.C: Applying warm compresses to the legs
options.D: Encouraging plenty of fluids to stop sluggish blood

explanation: Fluid is key! Drinking enough water keeps the thick blood moving smoothly and prevents dangerous clots.

question: Why can a blood problem cause symptoms all over the body?

options.A: The lymphatic system traps blood proteins
options.B: Blood flows through every single organ system
options.C: Bone marrow is found in many bones
options.D: Blood cells change shape quickly in the air

explanation: Since blood travels everywhere in the body, when something is off with our blood components, it can show up as tiredness, weakness, or bruising anywhere.

question: Why do unhealthy (malodaptive) coping strategies backfire in the end?

options.A: They make the body immune to all future stress hormones
options.B: They only offer temporary relief and often create new problems
options.C: They immediately cure physical diseases but ruin mental health
options.D: They cost too much money for ordinary community members

explanation: Hiding behind quick fixes might feel good for a minute, but it usually leaves the original problem untouched while adding fresh troubles.

question: A patient who received a light sedative for a joint scan is awake and asking to go home. What must you confirm before discharge?

options.A: That all physical pain in the joint has completely disappeared
options.B: That the patient has successfully voided a large amount of radioactive urine
options.C: That the radiologist has already completed the final written diagnostic report
options.D: That the patient has stable vital signs, a clear airway, and a responsible escort home

explanation: Sedatives can mess with a person's reflexes and clear thinking for hours. Always make sure they have stable vitals and a trusted adult to take them home safely.

question: What does the clinician usually do right before cutting the skin with the scalpel?

options.A: Elevating a small cone of skin using a sterile needle
options.B: Applying deep pressure to stop all local circulation
options.C: Stretching the skin tightly in four opposite directions
options.D: Massaging the area vigorously to numb it faster

explanation: Correct! Lifting a tiny tent of skin helps the clinician snip just the right top layer safely without cutting too deep.

question: What is the main goal of program implementation in community health?

options.A: Putting planned health interventions into actual practice
options.B: Gathering baseline data before designing an intervention
options.C: Writing the initial budget proposal for a health project
options.D: Assessing the long-term impact of a finished program

explanation: Implementation is all about action! It means taking the written plan and making it happen out there in the community where people need care.

question: What is the main reason a doctor performs a fine-needle aspiration (FNA) biopsy on a thyroid lump?

options.A: To obtain cells for microscopic examination to check for cancer
options.B: To inject radioactive isotopes directly into the thyroid tissue
options.C: To completely remove the entire thyroid gland without surgery
options.D: To measure the 24-hour baseline hormone production levels

explanation: Spot on! An FNA takes a tiny sample of cells so the lab can check them under a microscope to confirm or rule out cancer.

question: Why is good room ventilation important when mixing or using strong chemical disinfectants?

options.A: To prevent dust particles from settling into open chemical buckets
options.B: To keep room temperatures low so the disinfectant does not freeze
options.C: To speed up the chemical drying time on large operating tables
options.D: To prevent toxic fumes from accumulating and causing respiratory irritation

explanation: Strong chemical vapors can hurt your lungs and throat if the room isn't well-aired out. Breathe easy by keeping windows or vents open!

question: Why is twisting your body while lifting a heavy patient a big risk?

options.A: It puts uneven stress on the spinal discs
options.B: It cuts off circulation in the legs
options.C: It immediately lowers the patient's blood pressure
options.D: It causes the nurse to drop the patient's legs

explanation: Twisting while carrying weight puts awkward pressure on your spine, which is a quick way to get a bad back injury. Always pivot with your feet instead!

question: An Alzheimer's patient gets very confused every late afternoon. Which nursing action helps best?

options.A: Restrict all fluid intake after noon to prevent bathroom trips
options.B: Establish a calm, predictable daily routine with engaging daytime activities
options.C: Change the patient's daily care schedule constantly to keep them alert
options.D: Keep the room dark and quiet all day to encourage deep rest

explanation: Spot on! Predictable routines and daytime activities help prevent 'sundowning' (late-day confusion) by keeping them secure and engaged. Great care planning!

question: Why is an efficient food distribution system vital for community health?

options.A: It ensures steady access to affordable and nourishing food
options.B: It guarantees that all crops are grown using organic methods
options.C: It stops farmers from selling their produce in local markets
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for agricultural subsidies

explanation: When distribution works well, communities receive a consistent supply of food, which prevents shortages and protects public nutrition. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T025#GNS227_U2_T025_h1)

question: Why are elderly patients at much higher risk for brain-related side effects from anticholinergic drugs?

options.A: Their kidneys flush out the medication way too fast
options.B: Their bodies make way too much natural acetylcholine
options.C: They don't have any muscarinic receptors left in their body
options.D: Their blood-brain barrier is more sensitive and lets more drug through

explanation: You nailed it. Older adults are much more prone to confusion and fuzziness from these drugs because their brains and nervous systems handle these shifts more sensitively.

question: Which hormone is mainly responsible for pushing those delicate inner cervical cells outward?

options.A: Estrogen
options.B: Thyroxine
options.C: Insulin
options.D: Progesterone

explanation: Estrogen is the key player here! High levels of estrogen stimulate the inner cervical cells to grow and push outward onto the surface. Great job remembering your reproductive hormones.

question: Why is good communication among home health team members so vital?

options.A: It prevents conflicting instructions and ensures safe, coordinated care
options.B: It eliminates the need for any documentation or record keeping
options.C: It ensures that doctors do all the work without nursing assistance
options.D: It allows team members to compete for the patient's attention

explanation: Brilliant! When everyone shares updates, we avoid giving the patient confusing or mixed advice. Keep up the great work!

question: Which type of bacterial toxin is released only when the bacterial cell wall breaks apart?

options.A: Exotoxins
options.B: Coagulase
options.C: Endotoxins
options.D: Antitoxins

explanation: Endotoxins stay tucked inside the outer wall of certain bacteria (Gram-negative) and are only set free when the bacteria break down.

question: What is a major risk of spending too much time under strong ultraviolet (UV) sunlight?

options.A: Faster regeneration of damaged subcutaneous tissue
options.B: Enhanced production of protective surface lipids
options.C: Increased risk of skin cancers and premature aging
options.D: Permanent increase in the skin's moisture content

explanation: Correct! UV rays mess with skin cell DNA, which over time can cause early wrinkles and serious skin growths.

question: How do somatic motor pathways typically reach their target muscles?

options.A: They operate completely without you ever knowing
options.B: They use a two-neuron chain with a ganglion in the middle
options.C: They only stimulate internal glands and organs
options.D: They use a single direct neuron straight to the muscle

explanation: That's right! Somatic pathways take a straight, fast path from the spinal cord straight to the skeletal muscle with no stops in between.

question: What is the main purpose of the Child Rights Act passed in Nigeria in 2003?

options.A: Setting retirement ages for civil servants
options.B: Managing federal highway construction
options.C: Legal protection for child survival, development, and protection
options.D: Regulating international trade tariffs

explanation: The Child Rights Act domesticates international laws to ensure every Nigerian child is legally protected from abuse, neglect, and exploitation.

question: What is the main reason we usually apply creams or ointments directly to the skin?

options.A: To bypass the digestive tract entirely
options.B: To achieve a localized effect at the site
options.C: To replace intravenous fluid therapy
options.D: To provide rapid systemic distribution

explanation: Most topical creams are meant to work right where you put them—treating skin issues locally without flooding the whole body with medicine. You've got this!

question: Which blood tests are most vital for tracking complications in a patient with severe, ongoing watery stools?

options.A: Liver enzyme panel and lipid profile
options.B: Serum electrolytes and renal function tests
options.C: Fast blood glucose and glycosylated hemoglobin
options.D: Cardiac troponin levels and clotting times

explanation: Diarrhoea washes away key electrolytes like sodium and potassium, and can stress the kidneys. Checking electrolytes and kidney function helps us catch imbalances early!

question: What is the single most effective way to stop infections from spreading between patients in a ward?

options.A: Closing the windows to keep outdoor dust away
options.B: Consistent and proper hand hygiene by all staff
options.C: Burning all hospital bedsheets after a single use
options.D: Using scented air fresheners in the delivery room

explanation: You nailed it! Good hand hygiene is the number one defense against hospital-acquired infections.

question: Which nursing action prevents skin damage (shear forces) when moving a patient up in bed?

options.A: Using a draw sheet to lift the patient slightly off the mattress
options.B: Applying heavy lotion to the patient's heels and sacrum
options.C: Pulling the patient quickly by their ankles across the sheets
options.D: Lowering the head of the bed completely flat before moving

explanation: Always lift, never drag! A draw sheet prevents friction that can tear delicate skin layers against the bed sheet.

question: Which family planning method gives you dual protection against both pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections (STIs)?

options.A: Subdermal implants
options.B: Oral contraceptive pills
options.C: Intrauterine devices
options.D: Condoms

explanation: That's right! Barrier methods like male and female condoms block both sperm and infections, making them the only modern contraceptives that offer dual protection.

question: A nurse notices that teenage patients look nervous and hesitant when entering the consultation room. What immediate action should the nurse take?

options.A: Refuse to examine the patient until an older family member arrives
options.B: Scold the teenager for being afraid of a routine medical checkup
options.C: Use a warm tone and a welcoming posture to help put the teen at ease
options.D: Insist that a security guard stays inside the room during the interview

explanation: A welcoming attitude and friendly demeanor help break down anxiety and build trust with young clients. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h6)

question: A patient with advanced kidney disease has high potassium levels in their blood. Which local fruit should you advise them to limit?

options.A: Plain clear water and herbal tea
options.B: Unsalted butter and cooking oils
options.C: Ripe bananas and fresh oranges
options.D: White refined flour and table sugar

explanation: Bananas and oranges are loaded with potassium! When the kidneys aren't working well, extra potassium can cause dangerous heart rhythm problems. Always good to know.

question: How is oogenesis in females different from spermatogenesis in males?

options.A: Oogenesis continues at a rapid pace throughout old age
options.B: Oogenesis begins before birth and has a fixed supply of cells
options.C: Spermatogenesis produces fewer functional gametes over a lifetime
options.D: Spermatogenesis undergoes lengthy periods of meiotic arrest

explanation: You've got this! Unlike men who make new sperm all their lives, baby girls are born with all the eggs they will ever have.

question: What is the primary goal of prescribing cholinesterase inhibitors for a patient with Alzheimer's disease?

options.A: To completely reverse the formation of brain plaques
options.B: To temporarily manage symptoms and support daily function
options.C: To cure the underlying disease process within a few weeks
options.D: To prevent the patient from ever experiencing depression

explanation: These medications help boost chemical messengers in the brain to slow down symptom worsening, but they do not cure or reverse the disease. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T2#GNS222_U4_T2_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a sign that a uterine perforation might have happened?

options.A: Sudden relief from all abdominal cramping
options.B: Tenderness across the lower abdomen
options.C: Severe and worsening lower abdominal pain
options.D: Signs of internal bleeding and low blood pressure

explanation: A perforated uterus causes worsening pain and tenderness—not sudden relief! Always watch out for sharp abdominal pain after instrumentation.

question: How does harsh domestic discipline generally affect a teenager's behavior and safety?

options.A: It successfully prevents all forms of future accidental trauma
options.B: It increases the likelihood of risky behaviors and emotional distress
options.C: It improves the adolescent's ability to assess long-term danger
options.D: It has no measurable impact on mental or physical health

explanation: Great thinking! Harsh discipline and unstable homes raise stress levels, which are linked to higher rates of behavioral issues and injuries.

question: Why do we check baseline blood tests before starting certain tricky medications?

options.A: They prevent the drug from causing stomach irritation
options.B: They prove whether the patient has an active drug allergy
options.C: They provide a reference point to catch early organ damage
options.D: They calculate the exact lethal dose for that individual

explanation: Baselines give us a 'before' picture so we can quickly spot if a drug starts harming organs later. Brilliant nursing practice!

question: A patient says their knee pain gets worse when climbing stairs and feels better when resting. Which part of PQRST is this?

options.A: Pain severity and scale
options.B: Timing and frequency
options.C: Provoking and palliating factors
options.D: Region and radiation

explanation: Well done! Things that trigger pain (like stairs) are provoking factors, and things that soothe it (like rest) are palliating factors.

question: Why can having different professional goals cause friction between hospital management and bedside nurses?

options.A: Because differing priorities make each group feel the other is doing things wrong
options.B: Because hospital regulations forbid nurses from talking to administrators
options.C: Because managers want patients to stay in the hospital as long as possible
options.D: Because bedside nurses do not care about hospital budgets

explanation: When management focuses on quick patient turnover and bedside nurses focus on deep clinical care, their differing priorities can make them misunderstand each other.

question: What is the big advantage of organizing healthcare into different levels (primary, secondary, tertiary)?

options.A: It makes primary health clinics responsible for major surgical operations
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for any communication between nurses and doctors
options.C: It restricts rural clients from ever accessing modern contraceptive methods
options.D: It ensures clients receive care at the appropriate facility matching their medical complexity

explanation: Leveling care makes sure simple things are handled locally, while complex cases go smoothly to places fully equipped for them.

question: Sudden, heavy weight gain in the second half of pregnancy usually points to what?

options.A: Rapid increase in maternal muscle mass
options.B: Normal development of twin fetuses
options.C: Fluid retention or gestational hypertension
options.D: Excellent absorption of dietary protein

explanation: Spot on! If the scale jumps suddenly along with swelling, it's a red flag for water retention or high blood pressure issues.

question: What happens when a germ changes its target binding site?

options.A: The drug can no longer attach to the microbe effectively
options.B: The drug becomes toxic to human liver cells
options.C: The microbe begins producing extra doses of the antibiotic
options.D: The human immune system destroys the bacterial cell wall

explanation: Drugs need to lock onto a specific part of a pathogen to work. If the microbe alters that shape, the drug just slides right past!

question: A nurse is about to start an intravenous line for a patient with no known infections. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Put on a heavy rubber apron and shoe covers
options.B: Move the patient to an airborne isolation room
options.C: Ask the patient to wear a surgical mask
options.D: Perform hand hygiene and put on gloves

explanation: Standard precautions require hand hygiene and gloves before any procedure involving potential contact with blood or body fluids. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h3)

question: A hospital pharmacy keeps cash from drug sales in an open drawer and uses it to buy office snacks, leading to empty shelves. Which part of the DRF system is failing?

options.A: Quantification and forecasting
options.B: Manufacturing of raw chemicals
options.C: Revenue collection and banking
options.D: Patient disease diagnosis

explanation: Makes total sense, right? If cash isn't banked safely and gets spent on snacks, the revolving fund stops revolving, and drugs run out!

question: How do you acquire knowledge through the empirical method?

options.A: Through direct observation and sensory experience
options.B: Through pure logical thought without looking at the patient
options.C: By accepting traditional beliefs without testing
options.D: By waiting for a sudden gut feeling or intuition

explanation: Empiricism means gathering facts using your own senses—like looking at a wound, touching a pulse, or listening to lung sounds.

question: Why might a patient show signs of a delayed transfusion reaction a few days after getting blood?

options.A: The patient forgot to take prescribed post-transfusion antibiotics
options.B: Low-level antibodies increased over time and attacked newly introduced cells
options.C: The blood bag was stored in a refrigerator that was too cold
options.D: The intravenous cannula was left in place for too many days

explanation: Sometimes antibodies are so low in number that lab tests miss them initially. Once exposed to the donor cells, those antibody levels rise and start a delayed attack.

question: Why would a nurse use a Doppler ultrasound gadget during a physical checkup?

options.A: To check the patient's blood glucose level through the skin
options.B: To view the internal valves of veins using radioactive dye
options.C: To measure the exact electrical activity inside the heart muscle
options.D: To detect difficult-to-palpate peripheral pulses using sound waves

explanation: If a pulse is too faint to feel with your fingers, a Doppler uses sound waves to let you hear the 'whoosh' of blood flow loud and clear. Great tool!

question: Why do busy primary health centers often use syndromic management for sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: It guarantees that laboratory scientists are no longer needed in hospitals
options.B: It allows nurses to treat common symptoms immediately using flowcharts before lab results return
options.C: It completely replaces the need for any physical examination of the patient
options.D: It is the only method approved by international pharmaceutical companies

explanation: Brilliant! Syndromic management uses clear symptom guides so nurses can start treatment right away, which is a lifesaver when lab results take too long.

question: What happens if a standard ORS packet is mixed with way too little water?

options.A: It tastes better and is easier for babies to swallow
options.B: It creates a hypertonic solution that worsens dehydration
options.C: It neutralizes stomach acid more rapidly
options.D: It becomes more effective at curing the infection

explanation: If there's too little water, the mixture becomes too salty and concentrated, actually pulling more water out of the body's tissues into the gut!

question: A patient calls reporting a fever of 38.5°C and severe pelvic pain three days after a medical abortion. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: An ongoing uterine infection
options.B: An allergic reaction to ibuprofen
options.C: A normal side effect of mifepristone
options.D: A normal reaction to lingering hormones

explanation: Spot on! A lingering fever and severe pain days after the procedure can signal a uterine infection that needs a doctor's attention and antibiotics.

question: What is a big clinical plus of using biphasic defibrillators over monophasic ones?

options.A: They automatically treat both shockable and non-shockable rhythms
options.B: They achieve success with lower energy levels and less tissue injury
options.C: They do not require any conductive gel pads on the chest
options.D: They can deliver shocks safely through wet clothing

explanation: Because biphasic shocks work so well, we don't need as much electricity. This keeps the patient safer by lowering the risk of skin burns and heart muscle damage.

question: What often happens over time if juvenile delinquency is left unaddressed?

options.A: Automatic entry into high-ranking government leadership roles
options.B: Transition into chronic adult criminal behavior and incarceration
options.C: Spontaneous recovery without any impact on adult life
options.D: Complete immunity to all forms of physical and mental illness

explanation: Correct! Without early help and intervention, young people in trouble with the law often grow up to become adult offenders.

question: Why is unreliable electricity such a major threat to a clinic's immunization program?

options.A: It causes rapid expiration of dry vaccine powder inside sealed glass ampoules
options.B: It disables digital record books stored on desktop computers
options.C: It causes temperature fluctuations in vaccine refrigerators that destroy potency
options.D: It prevents nurses from turning on clinic lights during daytime immunizations

explanation: Power cuts mean unstable fridge temperatures, which can quietly spoil vaccines without anyone noticing until it's too late.

question: A patient catches malaria after being bitten by an infected mosquito. How would you classify this transmission?

options.A: Direct contact transmission
options.B: Airborne transmission
options.C: Vector-borne transmission
options.D: Vehicle-borne transmission

explanation: Mosquitoes, ticks, and other living creatures that carry germs to us are called vectors. That makes this a classic vector-borne disease!

question: Why is a microdrip tubing set (60 gtt/mL) often chosen for infants or sensitive pediatric patients?

options.A: It eliminates the need to use an electronic infusion pump entirely.
options.B: It pumps fluids at a much faster speed than standard gravity tubing.
options.C: It allows for much smaller, more precise adjustments in fluid delivery.
options.D: It prevents air bubbles from ever entering the patient's bloodstream.

explanation: Microdrip sets produce tiny drops, making it easier to deliver precise fluid volumes and prevent accidental fluid overload in small patients. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T16#GNS122_U1_T16_h6)

question: How should you support a joint while doing passive range of motion exercises?

options.A: Placing your hands above and below the joint
options.B: Letting the limb dangle freely without support
options.C: Holding the joint tightly right at its center point
options.D: Pulling firmly on the fingers or toes

explanation: Great job! Cradling the joint with hands positioned above and below gives solid support and protects the surrounding tissue.

question: A 30-week pregnant woman comes to the clinic complaining of a severe headache and blurred vision. What is your very first nursing action?

options.A: Discharge her home with instructions to eat more salt
options.B: Assess her blood pressure for signs of dangerous hypertension
options.C: Schedule her for routine tetanus vaccination next month
options.D: Encourage her to walk around the ward to improve circulation

explanation: Well done! Severe headaches and vision changes are classic danger signs of preeclampsia. Checking her blood pressure right away is a life-saving priority.

question: Why does hyperglycemia occur in patients with diabetes mellitus?

options.A: Dietary protein is converted directly into simple sugars
options.B: Cells fail to absorb glucose due to insulin problems
options.C: The kidneys actively produce excess glucose from water
options.D: The liver stores too much glycogen and refuses to release it

explanation: Without enough effective insulin, glucose cannot enter body cells for energy and instead stays building up in the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T13#GNS214_U1_T13_h1)

question: Which chemical messenger (neurotransmitter) is released by almost all autonomic preganglionic nerve fibers?

options.A: Epinephrine
options.B: Acetylcholine
options.C: Dopamine
options.D: Norepinephrine

explanation: Acetylcholine is the go-to chemical messenger used at the first synapse (ganglion) for both the sympathetic and parasympathetic divisions. Great job!

question: What are the two primary functions of the human nose?

options.A: Oxygenation and perfusion
options.B: Digestion and phonation
options.C: Respiration and olfaction
options.D: Filtration and circulation

explanation: The nose primarily functions as an airway for breathing (respiration) and as the sensory organ for smell (olfaction). [learn more](GNS211_U4_T3#GNS211_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why is getting male partners involved so important for family planning programs in Nigeria?

options.A: Male partners must administer all injectable contraceptives
options.B: Men often hold decision-making power regarding household health and finances
options.C: Hospitals legally prohibit women from buying contraception alone
options.D: Men are the only family members who suffer from reproductive infections

explanation: In many of our communities, men make the major household and financial decisions. If we leave them out of the conversation, family planning programs rarely succeed!

question: During which phase of development are haploid spermatids first formed?

options.A: Mitosis
options.B: Spermiogenesis
options.C: Capacitation
options.D: Meiosis

explanation: Meiosis is the special cell division that cuts the chromosome number in half, turning diploid cells into haploid spermatids.

question: What is the main goal of taking lifelong antiretroviral therapy (ART) for HIV?

options.A: To completely eliminate all dietary restrictions
options.B: To prevent the need for any future clinic visits
options.C: To successfully suppress the viral load
options.D: To permanently boost red blood cell counts

explanation: Keep it up! Taking medications daily keeps the virus under control, which protects the immune system and stops further transmission.

question: Which type of FGM involves removing the clitoris along with part or all of the labia minora?

options.A: Type I FGM
options.B: Type II FGM
options.C: Type IV FGM
options.D: Type III FGM

explanation: You've got this! Type II FGM is also called excision, where both the clitoris and labia minora are removed.

question: Why was the discovery of vitamins a massive turning point in healthcare?

options.A: It meant that eating enough total calories prevented all known illnesses
options.B: It eliminated the need for protein in the human diet
options.C: It proved diseases could happen simply from lacking small amounts of specific micronutrients
options.D: It showed that only wealthy people could ever suffer from nutritional disorders

explanation: Spot on! It opened our eyes to the fact that missing tiny trace elements, rather than just starving overall, could cause terrible diseases like scurvy.

question: What is the primary biological reason for the physical changes women feel during perimenopause?

options.A: Permanent closure of the cervical canal
options.B: Gradual depletion and decreased responsiveness of ovarian follicles
options.C: Complete failure of the anterior pituitary gland
options.D: Sudden permanent stoppage of all thyroid hormones

explanation: As the ovaries naturally run low on active egg follicles, estrogen and progesterone levels start rollercoasting before settling down.

question: How does vicarious liability work alongside a nurse's personal liability?

options.A: It completely replaces personal liability so the nurse can never be sued
options.B: It prevents the nursing council from investigating professional misconduct
options.C: It creates an additional layer of employer accountability without removing personal blame
options.D: It transfers all criminal charges from the nurse to the hospital director

explanation: Think of it as adding the hospital to the hot seat right beside you—it doesn't wipe away your own personal responsibility for the mistake.

question: What is the tiny working unit of the kidney that makes urine?

options.A: Neuron
options.B: Lobule
options.C: Alveolus
options.D: Nephron

explanation: You've got this! The nephron is the main filtering unit of the kidney that cleans the blood and creates urine. Think of millions of these little guys working hard inside each kidney.

question: Why are role-playing and peer education so effective in school health classes?

options.A: Students prefer playing games over reading textbooks
options.B: Interactive methods remove the need for qualified teachers
options.C: Government policies ban traditional classroom lecturing
options.D: Health habits are behavioral and require active practice

explanation: Spot on! Health education is all about changing daily actions, which works best when students actually practice what they are learning.

question: Why do typical natural family planning failure rates in real life end up higher than perfect-use rates?

options.A: Couples may occasionally miscalculate days or have intercourse during the fertile window
options.B: Prolactin levels fluctuate unpredictably in non-breastfeeding women
options.C: The body temperature thermometer loses accuracy over time
options.D: Hormones in natural methods expire quickly on store shelves

explanation: To err is human! Mistakes happen in real life—like misreading a chart or taking a chance on a fertile day—which raises the failure rate compared to textbook perfection.

question: You are giving bed bath care to an unconscious patient with a head injury. Which nursing action is most important?

options.A: Massaging the back vigorously to improve general circulation
options.B: Washing the face with cold water to stimulate consciousness
options.C: Removing the cervical collar to wash the neck thoroughly
options.D: Preventing sudden neck twisting and keeping the head aligned

explanation: Well done! Keeping the head and neck straight and neutral stops the neck veins from getting squeezed, which prevents sudden, dangerous spikes in brain pressure.

question: What is a primary responsibility of a nurse working in an assisted living facility?

options.A: Managing hospital emergency room admissions
options.B: Monitoring health status and coordinating care services
options.C: Running the facility financial and accounting department
options.D: Performing major surgical operations on-site

explanation: Assisted living nurses focus on health monitoring, wellness checks, and coordinating various support and medical services for the residents. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h4)

question: Which of the following does NOT happen during untreated status epilepticus?

options.A: Extremely high body temperature from muscle activity
options.B: Dangerous buildup of acid in the body fluids
options.C: Severe oxygen shortage and brain tissue damage
