options.D: Permanent drop in resting heart rate and low blood pressure

explanation: Correct! Instead of dropping, the heart rate and blood pressure actually shoot up due to extreme stress on the body. You're learning fast!

question: How does the sympathetic nervous system affect your pupils?

options.A: It causes dilation to let in more light
options.B: It causes involuntary blinking movements
options.C: It causes constriction to protect the retina
options.D: It has no direct effect on pupil size

explanation: When danger strikes, your pupils widen (dilate) so you can take in more visual details of your surroundings.

question: How does human relations theory change the daily role of a nurse manager?

options.A: Concentrating only on buying the cheapest medical supplies
options.B: Focusing on staff morale, communication, and teamwork
options.C: Enforcing strict obedience without listening to feedback
options.D: Eliminating all hospital policies to let staff do anything

explanation: Behavioral theories encourage managers to value employee input, build relationships, and support staff well-being. [learn more](GST321_U1_T3#GST321_U1_T3_h4)

question: What can happen if naloxone is pushed too fast into a patient who has been using opioids for a long time?

options.A: A sudden drop in heart rate leading to cardiac arrest
options.B: Immediate kidney failure and permanent anuria
options.C: Permanent paralysis of the skeletal muscles
options.D: Sudden and severe withdrawal symptoms like vomiting and agitation

explanation: While naloxone saves lives, pushing it too fast throws the patient straight into harsh withdrawal. They'll wake up throwing up and very agitated, so we push it carefully!

question: A mum at 28 weeks comes to the clinic with swollen face and high blood pressure. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: The fetus is growing at an unusually rapid and healthy rate
options.B: The mother is simply eating too much salt in her daily diet
options.C: This is a completely normal physical change in the third trimester
options.D: These are potential warning signs of preeclampsia requiring prompt evaluation

explanation: You nailed it! Sudden facial swelling plus high BP are red flags for preeclampsia. We always check these out immediately to keep the mum safe.

question: Why must nurses be extra careful when giving psychiatric drugs to patients with brain degeneration?

options.A: These drugs completely stop the physical progression of the genetic disease
options.B: Medications only work if they are given through an intravenous line
options.C: Their damaged brains make them more sensitive to side effects like excessive sedation
options.D: Patients with degenerative conditions are immune to all forms of chemical treatment

explanation: Brilliant. Because the central nervous system is altered, even small doses can cause strong side effects like heavy sleepiness. Always start low and go slow! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T13#GNS222_U4_T13_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT something food safety regulations normally check for?

options.A: Physical objects like metal shards or stones
options.B: Dangerous levels of chemical pesticide residues
options.C: Political views of the food manufacturing company owners
options.D: Harmful germs causing foodborne illnesses

explanation: Food safety is strictly about biological, chemical, and physical hazards—not who owns the company or what they believe!

question: What are the two primary functions of the ovaries during this monthly cycle?

options.A: Maturing follicles and producing sex hormones
options.B: Digesting fats and making red blood cells
options.C: Producing urine and filtering blood cells
options.D: Storing waste and regulating body temperature

explanation: The ovaries have a dual role of developing the female gametes inside follicles and secreting vital hormones like estrogen and progesterone. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T3#GNS216_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why might a survey show a very low prevalence for a mild skin condition that many people actually have?

options.A: Mild conditions automatically increase incidence instead of prevalence
options.B: Skin conditions cannot be measured using mathematical fractions
options.C: Government regulations forbid recording mild skin complaints
options.D: People may not seek care or report symptoms because the condition is mild

explanation: Unreported or undiagnosed mild illnesses are missed in surveys, leading to an underestimation of true prevalence. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h7)

question: What is the main goal of doing a secondary survey in critical care?

options.A: To administer routine scheduled morning drugs
options.B: To uncover hidden injuries or underlying problems
options.C: To discharge the patient from the hospital ward
options.D: To replace the need for laboratory blood tests

explanation: The head-to-toe secondary exam helps you find any sneaky injuries or issues that might have hidden during the fast primary survey.

question: What normal, harmless feeling do many patients report right after the contrast dye goes in?

options.A: A sharp, shooting pain down both legs
options.B: An intense urge to vomit large amounts of fluid
options.C: Sudden numbness in the fingertips and toes
options.D: A temporary flushing feeling and metallic taste

explanation: Don't panic! Feeling a sudden warm flush and tasting metal in the mouth are totally normal, everyday reactions to the dye.

question: What percentage of total semen volume is typically produced by the seminal vesicles?

options.A: About 60 percent
options.B: About 90 percent
options.C: About 10 percent
options.D: About 30 percent

explanation: The seminal vesicles contribute the majority of the fluid found in normal ejaculate. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T3#GNS121_U4_T3_h2)

question: Why should the nurse advise a patient to bring sunglasses to their ophthalmoscopy appointment?

options.A: Bright sunlight blocks the dilating drops from working properly
options.B: Dilated pupils let in excess light, causing glare and discomfort outdoors
options.C: Sunglasses protect the delicate contact lenses from blowing dust outside
options.D: The bright examination room light permanently damages unshielded eyes

explanation: Because dilating drops keep the pupil wide open, natural sunlight becomes overwhelmingly bright and uncomfortable for the patient. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h5)

question: Which diagnostic test specifically records the electrical activity of the brain?

options.A: Electrocardiogram (ECG)
options.B: Electroencephalogram (EEG)
options.C: Full blood count
options.D: Chest X-ray

explanation: An EEG uses electrodes placed on the scalp to detect and record abnormal electrical waves in the brain. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T11#GNS222_U4_T11_h5)

question: A patient complains of a burning pain in a leg that was surgically removed last week. How should you, as the nurse, respond?

options.A: Acknowledge the pain as real neuropathic discomfort and report it for treatment.
options.B: Tell the patient this feeling is temporary and will vanish within a few hours.
options.C: Suggest that the patient is imagining things because of anxiety over surgery.
options.D: Gently remind the patient that the leg is gone so the pain cannot actually exist.

explanation: Phantom pain is very real! It comes from the cut nerve endings trying to heal, so always validate your patient and get them the relief they need.

question: Which of the following is the best example of a SMART objective for a surgical ward?

options.A: Decrease surgical site infections by 10% over the next four months
options.B: Make sure the surgical ward is cleaner every single day
options.C: Try to be much nicer to patients during surgical admissions
options.D: Upgrade all hospital software before the end of the month

explanation: This statement is specific, measurable, realistic, relevant to clinical care, and has a clear deadline. [learn more](GST321_U2_T5#GST321_U2_T5_h4)

question: An adolescent health clinic welcomes all teenagers regardless of their financial status or background. Which core characteristic is this clinic showing?

options.A: Selective
options.B: Commercial
options.C: Exclusive
options.D: Equitable

explanation: Equitable care simply means fair treatment for every young person, treating everyone with equal care and without any form of discrimination.

question: Why must nurses always take complaints of menstrual pain seriously?

options.A: It is a legal requirement to report menstrual cramps to public health boards
options.B: Severe pain always indicates an underlying malignant tumour in the uterus
options.C: Menstrual pain is often dismissed despite being disabling for the patient
options.D: Pain during menstruation is extremely rare and requires immediate surgery

explanation: You got it! People often brush off menstrual cramps as 'normal,' so as nurses, our validation and compassionate care make a real difference.

question: Suddenly, a local government area sees a sharp, unexpected jump in measles cases. How would you classify this?

options.A: An endemic
options.B: A syndrome
options.C: An outbreak
options.D: A pandemic

explanation: Spot on! An outbreak is when we see a sudden, unexpected spike of disease cases in a specific, limited community.

question: In the famous 'Three Delays' model, what is the first delay all about?

options.A: The wait time to see a doctor at the hospital
options.B: The time spent traveling on bad rural roads
options.C: The decision by the family to seek medical help
options.D: The delay in manufacturing lifesaving drugs

explanation: Exactly right! The first delay happens right at home when family members take too long to recognize danger signs or decide it's time to visit a clinic.

question: Which lab tests do nurses commonly check to assess a patient's kidney function before giving medications?

options.A: Serum creatinine and BUN
options.B: ALT and AST liver enzymes
options.C: Red blood cell count and platelets
options.D: Sodium and potassium levels only

explanation: Blood Urea Nitrogen (BUN) and serum creatinine are your go-to lab markers. Checking these lets you know if the kidneys are clearing waste properly before piling on extra medications.

question: How do traditional community norms help keep early teenage marriage going?

options.A: By banning young women from working outside the home until they wed
options.B: By legally requiring all citizens to marry before completing secondary school
options.C: By viewing early marriage as a traditional marker of female honor and maturity
options.D: By offering free medical care exclusively to married teenage girls

explanation: Culture often links early marriage with family honor and good character, putting strong pressure on families to follow tradition.

question: Which action is strictly forbidden when handling used injection needles to prevent injuries?

options.A: Recapping needles by hand
options.B: Placing needles in a puncture-resistant bin
options.C: Reporting a sharps stick immediately
options.D: Carrying a tray with a used syringe

explanation: Correct! Never recap needles by hand—it's a leading cause of accidental needlestick injuries in the clinic.

question: Which method of getting rid of unwanted liquid medications is strongly discouraged because it pollutes water?

options.A: Returning them to the central pharmacy
options.B: Placing them in sealed pharmaceutical bins
options.C: Incinerating them in specialized facilities
options.D: Flushing them down the sink or toilet

explanation: Never flush medications down the drain! It carries active chemicals straight into public water sources and damages our ecosystem.

question: Where is the gray matter located in the cross-section of the spinal cord?

options.A: Directly outside the dura mater
options.B: Inside the central canal fluid
options.C: On the outer surface as tracts
options.D: On the inside in an H-shape

explanation: Unlike the brain where gray matter is on the outside, the spinal cord places its gray matter on the inside surrounded by white matter. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T3#GNS211_U3_T3_h6)

question: Which of these actions is an example of environmental source reduction to prevent malaria?

options.A: Taking daily anti-malarial tablets prescribed by a doctor
options.B: Draining stagnant puddles of water around the residential compound
options.C: Treating infected patients with intravenous fluid therapy
options.D: Getting vaccinated against mosquito-borne viral infections

explanation: Spot on! Source reduction is about removing the breeding grounds—like clearing out stagnant water where mosquitoes love to lay eggs.

question: During a hysterosalpingography (HSG) procedure, what is injected into the uterus to make the tubes visible on an X-ray?

options.A: Sterile normal saline
options.B: Liquid medical silicone
options.C: Radioactive glucose solution
options.D: Radiopaque contrast dye

explanation: Doctors use a special contrast dye so that X-ray machines can clearly trace the fluid as it flows through the womb and down the fallopian tubes.

question: What is a key safety duty for a nurse when giving a patient a new walking aid?

options.A: Disassembling the device daily for thorough cleaning
options.B: Painting the device to match the patient's favorite color
options.C: Restricting the patient from using it outside the hospital
options.D: Ensuring proper fit and teaching safe usage techniques

explanation: Safety first! If a walking aid doesn't fit right or isn't used properly, it can easily lead to accidental falls or injuries.

question: What is the main job of capillaries in our blood circulation?

options.A: Exchanging gases and nutrients with body tissues
options.B: Storing extra blood volume during rest
options.C: Carrying blood away from the heart under high pressure
options.D: Preventing blood from flowing backward in the legs

explanation: Capillaries are super tiny vessels with very thin walls. This allows oxygen, food nutrients, and waste to pass easily between your blood and your body tissues!

question: Why does the National Essential Medicines List divide drugs by levels of healthcare (like PHCs vs teaching hospitals)?

options.A: To restrict advanced medical care exclusively to politicians and the wealthy
options.B: To match drug availability with the clinical competence and needs of each facility type
options.C: To ensure that primary health centers have the most expensive drugs first
options.D: To make record-keeping as difficult as possible for rural nurses

explanation: Spot on! Basic health centers stock what nurses can safely give, while complex specialist drugs go to advanced teaching hospitals.

question: What do we call a sudden poisoning that happens right after a person has one large exposure to a chemical?

options.A: Acute exposure
options.B: Chronic exposure
options.C: Dermal accumulation
options.D: Systemic absorption

explanation: You've got this! Acute exposure simply means a one-time, short contact with a substance that quickly leads to symptoms or harm. Think of it as a sudden event, unlike chronic exposure which builds up over a long time.

question: What two things must be true for the rule of 'respondeat superior' to apply to a nurse's mistake?

options.A: An employer-employee relationship and action within the scope of employment
options.B: Written hospital policies and a signed malpractice insurance contract
options.C: A nursing license renewal and membership in a professional association
options.D: Direct supervision by a physician and a formal patient consent form

explanation: For the hospital to be pulled in, you must actually work there, and the mistake has to happen while you are doing your assigned job duties.

question: When prioritizing community health problems, what does 'magnitude' refer to?

options.A: The physical size of the primary health care clinic
options.B: The number of people in the community affected by the problem
options.C: The severity of pain caused by a specific injury
options.D: The monetary cost of purchasing medical equipment

explanation: Magnitude measures the scale or frequency of the health issue, specifically how large a percentage of the population is suffering from it. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h8)

question: Why is health education such an important part of maternal and child nursing?

options.A: It empowers mothers to recognize danger signs and seek timely care
options.B: It ensures that mothers do not visit traditional birth attendants
options.C: It reduces the need for nurses to document patient visits
options.D: It replaces the need for medical checkups during pregnancy

explanation: Wonderful! When mums know what warning signs to look out for, they can report back early and save lives.

question: Why do hospitals nowadays rarely give whole blood to patients?

options.A: Whole blood carries no oxygen-carrying capacity
options.B: Patients usually only need specific blood components
options.C: Whole blood spoils within two hours of collection
options.D: Processing whole blood is too expensive for hospitals

explanation: Great job thinking like a clinician! Blood is separated into parts so patients get precisely what they lack—like just red cells or platelets—rather than getting components they don't need.

question: What is recognized as the single most effective nursing action to prevent the spread of infections?

options.A: Administering broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.B: Spraying chemical disinfectants on floors
options.C: Frequent and proper hand hygiene
options.D: Placing all patients in isolation rooms

explanation: Handwashing and hand sanitizing remove transient microorganisms from the skin, preventing their transfer to patients. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T6#GNS313_U1_T6_h8)

question: Why is it important for nurses to understand healthcare laws?

options.A: To avoid personal liability and protect patient rights in clinical settings
options.B: To replace hospital lawyers during lawsuits
options.C: To prescribe medications independently when doctors are absent
options.D: To bypass getting consent from family members in emergencies

explanation: You got it! Knowing your legal boundaries helps you deliver safe care while keeping your license and patients protected.

question: Which organ problems make giving synergistic drugs especially risky?

options.A: Skin or muscle impairment
options.B: Liver or kidney impairment
options.C: Eye or ear impairment
options.D: Spleen or gallbladder impairment

explanation: Our liver and kidneys clear drugs out of our system. If they aren't working well, synergistic drugs can build up and reach toxic levels.

question: Why is taking rifampicin (for TB) alongside certain HIV drugs tricky?

options.A: It causes severe allergic skin rashes in all patients
options.B: Rifampicin alters liver enzymes and can lower antiretroviral blood levels
options.C: Rifampicin stops the absorption of water in the stomach
options.D: The combination immediately destroys the patient's pancreas

explanation: You got it! Rifampicin speeds up liver enzymes so much that it can flush HIV drugs out of the blood too quickly, risking treatment failure.

question: Why is a renal ultrasound often ordered when evaluating a patient with sudden kidney failure?

options.A: To test how well the liver is metabolizing circulating medications
options.B: To measure the exact amount of protein lost in a 24-hour period
options.C: To check for physical blockages or structural causes of urine backup
options.D: To determine the precise percentage of red blood cells in circulation

explanation: An ultrasound provides a clear image of the kidneys and urinary tract, helping doctors quickly identify postrenal obstructions like stones or an enlarged prostate. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T6#GNS213_U4_T6_h4)

question: Which reflex is NOT coordinated by the medulla oblongata?

options.A: The swallowing reflex
options.B: The coughing reflex
options.C: The vomiting reflex
options.D: Visual tracking of a moving object

explanation: Visual tracking is handled by higher brain areas and midbrain structures, whereas vomiting, swallowing, and coughing are medullary reflexes. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h5)

question: According to the World Health Organization (WHO), what age range covers adolescents and youths?

options.A: 5 to 12 years
options.B: 25 to 40 years
options.C: Birth to 5 years
options.D: 10 to 24 years

explanation: You got this! International health guidelines define the adolescent and youth bracket as spanning from 10 to 24 years. It's a vital transition phase you'll see often in community nursing.

question: Why must a client eat a diet rich in carbohydrates for three days before a GTT?

options.A: To make sure the stomach is completely full before drinking the sweet syrup
options.B: To prevent false-positive results caused by low carbohydrate intake
options.C: To test how fast the liver can store extra glycogen reserves
options.D: To ensure the patient has plenty of energy to sit still during the test

explanation: If a patient restricts carbs beforehand, their body stops producing enough insulin, causing a fake diabetic spike during the test. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T20#GNS222_U2_T20_h3)

question: Why should community nurses use simple everyday language and live demonstrations during health talks?

options.A: To discourage people from asking questions during lectures
options.B: To ensure clear understanding and encourage practical application by listeners
options.C: To make the teaching session take as little time as possible
options.D: To hide complex medical terminology from uneducated citizens

explanation: Exactly! Keeping it simple ensures everyone follows along and can actually practice what they learned when they go home.

question: What is the direct result of acetylcholine binding to receptors on the motor end plate?

options.A: Calcium ions are pumped out of the cell
options.B: Sodium ions rush into the muscle fiber
options.C: The nerve ending absorbs the muscle cell
options.D: Myosin heads detach from the actin filaments

explanation: ACh opens chemically gated channels, letting sodium flood inward to start the electrical action potential in the muscle cell. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h5)

question: Why do nurses love recommending condoms as a first-line protection tool?

options.A: They alter the body's natural hormone levels
options.B: They require a doctor's prescription
options.C: They protect against both pregnancy and infections
options.D: They offer permanent sterilization

explanation: Spot on! Condoms give you dual protection—they stop unwanted pregnancy and keep sexually transmitted infections away at the same time.

question: You are getting instruments ready for a deep abdominal surgery. How must these tools be processed?

options.A: Low-level disinfection
options.B: Sterilization
options.C: High-level disinfection
options.D: Thorough soap washing

explanation: Any tool going into sterile body tissue or blood vessels is a critical item and absolutely must be sterilized!

question: Why must nurses check for other physical symptoms alongside pain during a palliative assessment?

options.A: Multiple symptoms interact and can make each other worse, like breathlessness causing panic
options.B: Non-pain symptoms are usually much more dangerous than actual physical pain
options.C: Insurance companies only pay for care if three symptoms are treated at once
options.D: Doctors only look at pain scores and ignore all other bodily complaints

explanation: Symptoms don't happen in isolation. Struggling to breathe can trigger panic, so we need to look at the whole picture!

question: What is a vital nursing duty when caring for a pregnant mother with Type III infibulation?

options.A: Advising the patient that no special birth plan is required
options.B: Scheduling an elective hysterectomy at thirty-six weeks
options.C: Instructing the patient to perform self-suturing after delivery
options.D: Anticipating the need for defibulation to allow safe childbirth

explanation: Women with Type III infibulation often need a surgical procedure to open the scar tissue (defibulation) before or during labor so the baby can be born safely.

question: What common economic challenge often forces families to rely heavily on cheap, refined carbohydrate meals?

options.A: A total lack of agricultural land for farming throughout the entire country
options.B: Financial poverty that makes fresh vegetables and lean proteins expensive
options.C: Universal free distribution of processed foods at primary healthcare centres
options.D: Strict government bans on importing nutritious food items into local markets

explanation: You've got it. Economic reality plays a huge role in health. When fresh protein and veggies are pricey, families naturally turn to cheaper, filling carbs.

question: A child weighs 44 pounds. What is the child's weight in kilograms?

options.A: 20 kg
options.B: 22 kg
options.C: 44 kg
options.D: 88 kg

question: What must a nurse always do when a calculated safety box requirement results in a fractional number like 12.3 boxes?

options.A: Always round up to the next whole number.
options.B: Ignore the calculation and request an arbitrary box amount.
options.C: Discard the fraction and order only the exact whole integer.
options.D: Always round down to the nearest lower whole number.

explanation: Rounding up ensures you never run out of disposal containers for your used needles and syringes. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T13#GNS122_U3_T13_h5)

question: Which of the following is a normal age-related change in the cardiovascular system?

options.A: A permanent increase in the total volume of circulating red blood cells
options.B: Increased stiffness and reduced elasticity of the arterial walls
options.C: Rapid expansion and extreme thinning of the main heart valves
options.D: Complete cessation of electrical activity in the resting sinus node

explanation: As people age, blood vessels naturally become less flexible, which often leads to higher blood pressure readings. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T8#GNS225_U5_T8_h2)

question: What is the preferred, minimally invasive surgery for stable patients needing a look at their pelvic organs?

options.A: Thoracotomy
options.B: Cystoscopy
options.C: Total hysterectomy
options.D: Laparoscopy

explanation: Spot on! Laparoscopy uses tiny cuts and a camera, meaning less pain and a much faster recovery for the patient.

question: Which of the following is a non-modifiable risk factor for cancer?

options.A: Smoking
options.B: Alcohol use
options.C: Diet
options.D: Age

explanation: Age is an inherent biological factor that cannot be altered, making it non-modifiable. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why do nurses care about catching cervical irritation early?

options.A: It prevents simple discomfort from progressing to chronic or ascending infections.
options.B: It immediately normalizes hormonal fluctuations during the menstrual cycle.
options.C: It guarantees that surgical intervention will never be required.
options.D: It completely eliminates the future risk of all pelvic inflammatory diseases.

explanation: Exactly! Catching inflammation early stops it from traveling up into the upper reproductive tract where it can cause bigger problems.

question: What is the primary goal of injection safety in nursing practice?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing medical supplies
options.B: To ensure injections do no harm to the patient or worker
options.C: To speed up the administration of routine vaccinations
options.D: To eliminate the need for personal protective equipment

explanation: Injection safety focuses entirely on protecting patients, healthcare workers, and the community from injury and disease transmission during injection procedures. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T3#GNS122_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why is looking at a trend of vital signs over several hours so much better than just checking a single set of numbers?

options.A: It is required for billing and insurance records
options.B: It proves the machine is working properly
options.C: It shows the direction the patient's health is moving
options.D: It replaces the need for physician physical exams

explanation: Exactly! Tracking numbers over time helps you spot a slow, steady slip in a patient's condition, even if their current numbers still technically look 'normal.'

question: Which sign points to a MILD drug reaction rather than a severe one?

options.A: Itchy hives on the skin with normal breathing
options.B: A sudden drop in blood pressure and fainting
options.C: Swelling of the tongue and throat
options.D: Wheezing across both lungs

explanation: Mild reactions usually stay on the skin as simple itching or hives, leaving the airway and breathing completely safe.

question: A patient having a severe allergic reaction has wheezing, swollen lips, and crashing blood pressure. What medication is given first?

options.A: Intramuscular epinephrine
options.B: Oral diphenhydramine
options.C: Subcutaneous insulin
options.D: Intravenous paracetamol

explanation: Brilliant! Epinephrine is a lifesaver in anaphylaxis because it quickly opens up the airways and brings blood pressure back up.

question: A patient complains that constant hospital noise and glaring overhead lights won't let them sleep. What kind of stressor is this?

options.A: Environmental stressor
options.B: Eustress
options.C: Psychosocial stressor
options.D: Physiological stressor

explanation: Things around us in our physical surroundings—like annoying hospital sounds or bright lights—are environmental stressors. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T15#GNS123_U3_T15_h3)

question: Which of these actions is NOT allowed during a surgical hand scrub?

options.A: Using disposable picks to clean under your fingernails
options.B: Leaning against the sink edge to rest your arms
options.C: Keeping your hands higher than your elbows
options.D: Standing at a safe distance from the sink

explanation: Leaning against the sink transfers germs from your scrubs to your body, breaking sterility and forcing a re-scrub.

question: What main heart rhythm is an AED built to fix with an electrical shock?

options.A: Ventricular fibrillation
options.B: Sinus bradycardia
options.C: First-degree heart block
options.D: Atrial flutter

explanation: An AED is designed to step in during life-threatening rhythms like ventricular fibrillation, resetting the heart's electrical system so it can beat normally again.

question: Why is immediate reporting of unusual disease symptoms by a PHC nurse critical?

options.A: It triggers a rapid public health response to prevent an outbreak
options.B: It allows the nurse to close the clinic early for the week
options.C: It fulfills a routine paperwork requirement without clinical impact
options.D: It secures financial bonuses for the local clinic staff

explanation: Quick reporting allows health authorities to investigate early and stop infectious diseases from spreading widely. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T7#GNS124_U2_T7_h5)

question: Why is keeping a food diary helpful for someone with gas issues?

options.A: It completely cures lactose intolerance without any medication.
options.B: It measures the exact volume of gas produced each hour.
options.C: It helps the patient and nurse pinpoint specific foods that trigger excess gas.
options.D: It guarantees the patient will lose weight within the first week.

explanation: Writing down meals and symptoms helps connect the dots so patients can figure out which foods don't agree with them.

question: Why must a chest drainage system always be placed lower than the patient's chest?

options.A: To make it easier for the patient to walk around the unit
options.B: To ensure the water seal chamber bubbles continuously
options.C: To use gravity to keep fluid draining away from the pleural cavity
options.D: To prevent the suction regulator from breaking

explanation: You nailed it! Gravity is our helper here; keeping the canister low ensures fluid drains out of the chest and doesn't flow back in.

question: Under normal circumstances, how often should you check cervical dilation during active labour?

options.A: Once every 24 hours
options.B: Every 30 minutes
options.C: Every 4 hours
options.D: Every 15 seconds

explanation: Checking every 4 hours gives you a clear picture of how labour is advancing while keeping the risk of infection low.

question: According to the Health Belief Model, what must a patient believe first before they will change a health habit?

options.A: The government has implemented strict laws banning unhealthy food imports
options.B: Their local primary healthcare clinic is fully funded and well-equipped
options.C: Their family members have already suffered from the same chronic illness
options.D: They are personally vulnerable to the health condition and see benefits in changing

explanation: Correct! Patients won't change unless they genuinely believe "this can happen to me" and that taking action will actually make a difference for them.

question: A patient suddenly struggles to breathe and swells up after getting an antibiotic injection for the first time. What type of drug reaction is this?

options.A: Type A dose-dependent pharmacological reaction
options.B: Type D delayed teratogenic reaction
options.C: Type B idiosyncratic or allergic reaction
options.D: Type C chronic accumulation reaction

explanation: Brilliant! Anaphylaxis is a classic Type B reaction—it comes out of nowhere, has nothing to do with a high dose, and involves the immune system.

question: Why must nurses tailor assessment tools to fit a degenerative patient's physical limits?

options.A: To make the test results legally binding in a court of law
options.B: To eliminate the need for family members to be present
options.C: To ensure the patient does not get tired or frustrated during testing
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing paper questionnaires

explanation: If a patient is exhausted, test scores won't show their true ability. Matching their energy levels keeps the assessment accurate and stress-free.

question: What is the purpose of performing a bimanual examination right before an MVA starts?

options.A: To determine the exact size and position of the uterus
options.B: To scrape away loose tissue without needing a canula
options.C: To check if the patient's bladder is completely empty
options.D: To measure the patient's blood pressure and pulse rate

explanation: Knowing whether the uterus is tilted forward or backward helps the clinician guide instruments smoothly and prevents accidental perforation. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h5)

question: A patient's tray is empty, but you suspect they didn't eat. What might have happened?

options.A: Food may have been eaten by a visitor or spilled
options.B: Dietary intake only counts if a dietitian sees it
options.C: The kitchen staff forgot to put food on the plate
options.D: The patient's metabolism is moving too fast

explanation: Correct! An empty tray doesn't guarantee the patient ate the food. Always double-check before charting their intake.

question: Who should standard precautions be applied to in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Visitors entering the surgical ward
options.B: Patients with airborne illnesses only
options.C: Only patients with diagnosed HIV
options.D: All patients receiving care

explanation: Standard precautions are universal and apply to every patient, because infection status is not always known. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h3)

question: Which of the following is an important practice when buying packaged foods?

options.A: Selecting products with no ingredient labels listed
options.B: Choosing the can with the deepest rust spots for a discount
options.C: Buying items with the shortest remaining shelf life
options.D: Inspecting the package to ensure it is not torn or dented

explanation: Damaged packaging can let air and bacteria inside, spoiling the food and endangering the consumer's health. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T006#GNS227_U3_T006_h4)

question: You just finished changing a wound dressing and took off your gloves. What is your very next step?

options.A: Wait until leaving the client's home to wash the hands
options.B: Perform hand hygiene immediately after removing the gloves
options.C: Wipe hands with a dry cloth towel kept in the nursing bag
options.D: Apply hand lotion over the gloves before touching supplies

explanation: Always wash or sanitise right after taking off gloves! Tiny microscopic tears can let germs sneak through to your skin while you work.

question: What is the main way regular exposure to chemicals (like in certain workplaces) affects liver enzymes?

options.A: It completely stops all future cellular protein synthesis
options.B: It doubles the physical size and weight of the organ
options.C: It permanently turns the liver into hard scar tissue
options.D: It can either speed up or slow down their normal function

explanation: Chemical exposures can trick your liver. They either 'induce' (speed up) or 'inhibit' (slow down) the enzymes that break down everyday medicines. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T10#GNS125_U5_T10_h4)

question: How do global health organizations view female genital mutilation?

options.A: As an acceptable traditional surgical option
options.B: As a violation of basic human rights
options.C: As a mandatory rite of passage for health
options.D: As a minor procedure with minimal complications

explanation: Correct! Major health bodies view FGM as a serious violation of human rights and bodily safety for women and girls. Keep up the great work!

question: Why do we encourage skin-to-skin contact right after a normal delivery?

options.A: It completely prevents the mother from experiencing postpartum bleeding
options.B: It speeds up the surgical healing of an episiotomy wound
options.C: It acts as a permanent immunization against childhood illnesses
options.D: It helps regulate the newborn's body temperature and encourages breastfeeding

explanation: That's right! Mum's body heat keeps the baby warm, and it gets breastfeeding off to a great start.

question: What is the core philosophy of Primary Health Care (PHC)?

options.A: Bringing essential health services as close as possible to where people live
options.B: Focusing treatment exclusively on patients who can pay cash
options.C: Relying entirely on foreign medical aid for community survival
options.D: Building high-tech specialist hospitals in major metropolitan cities

explanation: PHC emphasizes grassroots accessibility, making basic health promotion and disease prevention available to everyone in the community. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h6)

question: Why are strong opioid painkillers usually avoided for routine home care after an abortion?

options.A: They carry high risks of sedation, nausea, and dependency
options.B: They permanently damage the lining of the stomach
options.C: They cause the uterus to stop contracting completely
options.D: They raise blood pressure to dangerously high levels

explanation: Routine cramps can usually be handled safely with milder drugs, sparing the patient from heavy side effects like sleepiness and nausea. Makes total sense!

question: Which fluid-filled cavity does the diencephalon surround?

options.A: The fourth ventricle near the pons
options.B: The lateral ventricles of the frontal lobes
options.C: The central canal of the spinal cord
options.D: The third cerebral ventricle

explanation: Spot on! The structures of the diencephalon form the walls and floor around the third ventricle to help circulate cerebrospinal fluid.

question: Which lung issue is most common for a patient stuck on prolonged bed rest in traction?

options.A: Hyperventilation syndrome
options.B: Asthma attack
options.C: Atelectasis
options.D: Spontaneous pneumothorax

explanation: Well done! Lying flat and breathing shallowly can cause small air sacs in the lungs to collapse (atelectasis). That's why deep breathing exercises and incentive spirometry are so important!

question: Which vitamin deficiency is the main cause of Korsakoff syndrome?

options.A: Niacin deficiency
options.B: Thiamine deficiency
options.C: Cobalamin deficiency
options.D: Ascorbic acid deficiency

explanation: Spot on! Korsakoff syndrome happens when the body lacks vitamin B1 (thiamine), which the brain really needs to keep memory working smoothly.

question: Why does the baby have to make 'cardinal movements' while coming down the birth canal?

options.A: To stimulate the release of oxytocin from the maternal pituitary gland
options.B: To speed up the latent phase of the first stage of labour
options.C: To prevent the umbilical cord from wrapping around the baby's neck
options.D: To help the fetal head fit through the changing shapes of the maternal pelvis

explanation: The pelvis isn't a straight pipe! The baby has to twist and turn to navigate the different curves safely.

question: What is usually the very first physical sign of puberty in young females?

options.A: Breast development
options.B: Growth of pubic hair
options.C: First menstrual period
options.D: Widening of the hips

explanation: Breast budding, known medically as thelarche, is typically the earliest visible sign that puberty has begun. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T6#GNS311_U1_T6_h4)

question: When is active health surveillance most useful in a community?

options.A: Only when tracking patients who move to another country
options.B: When health workers want to reduce their daily working hours
options.C: When the health clinic has no paper, pens, or staff available
options.D: During a disease outbreak or targeted immunization campaign

explanation: Active surveillance means rolling up your sleeves and going out to hunt for cases. We do this when there is an outbreak (like cholera or measles) and every single hour counts!

question: A patient reads Braille with their fingertips. Which receptor helps them feel those tiny raised dots?

options.A: Ruffini endings
options.B: Merkel discs
options.C: Free nerve endings
options.D: Pacinian corpuscles

explanation: Spot on! Merkel discs are slow-adapting receptors near the surface that excel at picking up fine details and textures.

question: Why should primary health care teams regularly review their defaulter tracing data?

options.A: To prove that no children ever miss their scheduled vaccines
options.B: To justify stopping immunization services in rural areas
options.C: To find persistent barriers and improve community outreach strategies
options.D: To punish health workers whose clinics have low coverage

explanation: Reviewing data helps health teams spot trends, fix recurring bottlenecks, and adapt their outreach to reach every child. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T74#GNS214_U1_T74_h6)

question: Why is catching conditions like chronic bowel diseases early so important?

options.A: It prevents long-term tissue scarring and organ damage
options.B: It guarantees the patient will never need any medication
options.C: It stops the digestive system from absorbing water
options.D: It eliminates all bacteria living inside the intestines

explanation: Catching issues early gives treatment a chance to slow things down and keep the organ from getting permanently scarred or damaged.

question: What is the main goal of a negative feedback loop in the body?

options.A: To trigger rapid nerve impulses during acute physical pain
options.B: To maintain hormone levels within a stable, normal range
options.C: To continuously amplify hormone production until exhaustion
options.D: To replace lost nutrients in the extracellular fluid

explanation: Think of negative feedback like an air conditioner: when the room gets too cold (or hormone levels get too high), it turns things off to keep balance.

question: Which part of the cell contains the genetic material or DNA?

options.A: The plasma membrane
options.B: The nucleus
options.C: The cytoplasm
options.D: The ribosome

explanation: The nucleus houses the cell's DNA, acting as the command center for instructions on building proteins and running cellular operations. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T5#GNS111_U1_T5_h2)

question: A mother visits the clinic with a four-month-old baby and asks about getting pregnant again immediately. What is your best nursing response regarding child health?

options.A: Tell her that child health has no connection to how close pregnancies are
options.B: Advise waiting at least two years to protect the health of both the baby and future children
options.C: Encourage immediate conception so the children can grow up as close friends
options.D: Suggest she stop breastfeeding immediately to prepare for the next pregnancy

explanation: Waiting helps ensure the current infant receives prolonged breastfeeding and reduces risks like malnutrition and infections. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h2)

question: How does better nutrition quietly boost a patient's overall quality of life?

options.A: By increasing their financial income through savings
options.B: By ensuring they never experience physical pain again
options.C: By giving them the energy to enjoy daily activities and hobbies
options.D: By making them sleep for twelve hours every night

explanation: Exactly! When chronic fatigue fades away, patients can finally get back to enjoying their daily walks, family gatherings, and favorite hobbies.

question: What should a polyvalent nurse do if standard supplies run out during an emergency?

options.A: Abandon the patient until fresh supplies arrive
options.B: Use problem-solving skills to find safe alternatives
options.C: Wait for the hospital director to fix the issue
options.D: Blame the junior nursing staff for the shortage

explanation: Well done! Resourcefulness is key in nursing. Finding safe alternatives keeps patients protected even when supplies are low.
